slides.title: Executive summary
points: Cloud spend reached 41.8 million euros in the last twelve months, which is 23 percent above the approved budget, and the overrun is concentrated in compute and data platform services in three business units.

Roughly a third of running compute is idle or oversized according to the utilisation scan in September, so rightsizing and scheduled shutdown of non-production estates is the largest and fastest savings lever.
Only 38 percent of steady-state workloads are covered by committed-use discounts today, compared to a benchmark of 70 to 80 percent, which leaves about 3.1 million euros of annual discount unclaimed.
Storage lifecycle policies are missing on most buckets and snapshots, so cold data sits on premium tiers, and moving it to archive classes would save about 1.4 million euros per year with low risk.
Nobody owns cost today because 44 percent of spend is untagged, so we propose a FinOps team of five with showback per product team and monthly budget reviews with each engineering director.
The programme delivers 9.6 million euros of annual run-rate savings within twelve months for a one-off investment of 1.2 million euros, and we ask the committee to approve option B today.

options.label: Option A: run a tactical clean-up of idle compute with the existing platform team
Option B: fund a FinOps programme with a team of five and a twelve-month mandate
Option C: re-platform the forty largest workloads to containers and serverless

steps.label: Baseline
steps.description: Build a complete and tagged inventory of all cloud resources across the three providers and reconcile it with the invoices of the last twelve months.

steps.label: Tag
steps.description: Enforce a mandatory tagging policy for owner, product and environment so that every euro of spend can be allocated to a product team.

steps.label: Rightsize
steps.description: Resize or terminate the instances that the utilisation scan identified as idle or oversized, starting with non-production environments.

steps.label: Schedule
steps.description: Introduce automatic shutdown schedules for development and test environments outside working hours and on weekends.

steps.label: Commit
steps.description: Purchase committed-use discounts and savings plans for the steady-state baseline once rightsizing has stabilised the footprint.

steps.label: Tier
steps.description: Apply lifecycle policies to object storage and snapshots so that cold data moves automatically to cheaper archive classes.

steps.label: Showback
steps.description: Publish monthly showback reports per product team and review variances against budget with each engineering director.

steps.label: Sustain
steps.description: Embed cost checks into the delivery pipeline and architecture reviews so that savings do not erode after the programme ends.
